title: The risen saints will be immortal in both senses, unlike Adam in innocence
source_text: IV. Unde colligi potest discrimen inter immortalitatem primi hominis in statu integritatis, & illam quae competet justis post beatam resurrectionem. Nam Sancti post resurrectionem nullo modo mortales erunt: nec enim solum immunes erunt a necessitate moriendi, sed prorsus mori non poterunt, & peccando mortem aut mortalitatem incurrere. Et ita immortales erunt utroque modo, quia non solum poterunt non mori, sed mori non poterunt, & mors non poterit unquam ullam in eos habere potestatem.
pass_a_gloss: Whence can be gathered the difference between the immortality of the first man in the state of integrity, and that which will belong to the just after the blessed resurrection. For the Saints after the resurrection will in no way be mortal: for not only will they be immune from the necessity of dying, but they will be wholly unable to die, and by sinning to incur death or mortality. And so they will be immortal in both ways, because not only will they be able not to die, but they will not be able to die, and death will never be able to have any power over them.
pass_b_english: From this one can see how the first man's immortality in the state of integrity differs from the immortality the just will have after the blessed resurrection.

After the resurrection the saints will not be mortal in any way. They will not only be free from the necessity of dying; they will be altogether unable to die, or to bring death or mortality on themselves by sinning. So they will be immortal in both senses: they will not only be able not to die, they will be unable to die, and death will never have any power over them.

choices.why: The non posse mori of the blessed, set against Adam's posse non mori.
